trans-unit.id: Air pollution output is divided by this to determine PPM. It depends on AtmospherePressureKgPerM2 and the world area. For 1km2 and pressure 1kg/m2, 1 ton = 1PPM (part per million), which is the unit that determines climate change effects.
trans-unit.source: Air pollution output is divided by this to determine PPM. It depends on AtmospherePressureKgPerM2 and the world area. For 1km2 and pressure 1kg/m2, 1 ton = 1PPM (part per million), which is the unit that determines climate change effects.
trans-unit.target: يتم تقسيم ناتج تلوث الهواء على هذا لتحديد جزء في المليون. ذلك يعتمد على AtmospherePressureKgPerM2 والمنطقة العالمية. بالنسبة إلى 1 كم 2 والضغط 1 كجم / م 2 ، 1 طن = 1PPM (جزء في المليون) ، وهي الوحدة التي تحدد تأثيرات تغير المناخ.

trans-unit.id: How much PPM (particles per million) will be added to/removed from atmosphere per one tone of matter (i.e. CO2).

trans-unit.target: مقدار جزء في المليون (جزيء لكل مليون) ستتم إضافته / إزالته من الغلاف الجوي لكل نغمة واحدة من المادة (مثل ثاني أكسيد الكربون).

trans-unit.id: Atmosphere pressure used in the atmosphere size formula. Trees absorb and pollution from tables produced in tons and converted to PPM by dividing on total atmosphere size. AtmosphereSizeInTons = WorldAreaInM2 * AtmospherePressureKgPerM2 where WorldAreaInM2 = (Dimensions.x * 10) * (Dimensions.y * 10). In example for 1km² (1000000m²) world with atmosphere pressure 1 kg/m² it will be 1000000 tons, resulting in 1 PPM per 1 ton of pollution or absorb (1 PPM = 1000000 * tons / AtmosphereSizeInTons), increasing pressure to 2 will result in 0.5 PPM per ton.
trans-unit.source: Atmosphere pressure used in the atmosphere size formula. Trees absorb and pollution from tables produced in tons and converted to PPM by dividing on total atmosphere size. AtmosphereSizeInTons = WorldAreaInM2 * AtmospherePressureKgPerM2 where WorldAreaInM2 = (Dimensions.x * 10) * (Dimensions.y * 10). In example for 1km² (1000000m²) world with atmosphere pressure 1 kg/m² it will be 1000000 tons, resulting in 1 PPM per 1 ton of pollution or absorb (1 PPM = 1000000 * tons / AtmosphereSizeInTons), increasing pressure to 2 will result in 0.5 PPM per ton.
trans-unit.target: الضغط الجوي المستخدم في صيغة حجم الغلاف الجوي. تمتص الأشجار وتتلوث من الجداول المنتجة بالأطنان وتحول إلى PPM عن طريق القسمة على إجمالي حجم الغلاف الجوي. AtmosphereSizeInTons = WorldAreaInM2 * AtmospherePressureKgPerM2 حيث WorldAreaInM2 = (Dimensions.x * 10) * (Dimensions.y * 10). على سبيل المثال ، بالنسبة لعالم 1 كيلومتر مربع (1000000 متر مربع) مع ضغط جوي 1 كجم / متر مربع ، سيكون 1000000 طن ، مما ينتج عنه 1 جزء في المليون لكل 1 طن من التلوث أو الامتصاص (1 جزء في المليون = 1000000 * طن / AtmosphereSizeInTons) ، يؤدي زيادة الضغط إلى 2 إلى 0.5 جزء في المليون للطن.

trans-unit.source: Your GPU's Max Tessellation Level is less than 64. trans-unit.target: الحد الأقصى لمستوى التغطية بالفسيفساء في وحدة معالجة الرسومات GPU أقل من 64. trans-unit.id: This setting defines how plants will be grouped when the world generates. It have two levels of grouping: clusters and groups. A cluster is a large area of the world where a particular type of plant exists, and it affects gameplay by limiting where specific plants can be spawned. Groups are primarily for visual purposes, so plants of the same species grow together with only a small distance between them.
trans-unit.source: This setting defines how plants will be grouped when the world generates. It have two levels of grouping: clusters and groups. A cluster is a large area of the world where a particular type of plant exists, and it affects gameplay by limiting where specific plants can be spawned. Groups are primarily for visual purposes, so plants of the same species grow together with only a small distance between them.
trans-unit.target: يحدد هذا الإعداد كيفية تجميع النباتات عند إنشاء العالم. وتوجد مستويان من التجميع: المجموعات والمجموعات الفرعية. المجموعة هي منطقة واسعة من العالم يوجد فيها نوع معين من النباتات، وتؤثر على طريقة اللعب من خلال تحديد الأماكن التي يمكن أن تنمو فيها نباتات معينة. أما المجموعات الفرعية فهي لأغراض بصرية في المقام الأول، بحيث تنمو نباتات من نفس النوع معًا مع وجود مسافة صغيرة فقط بينها.

trans-unit.id: How old records can be grouped. It means it will try to process all last X days of records to group them. Usually you want to have this number low (1-2) in order to avoid process already processed records, but you can set high value (by example world age) in order to process at once all records from some old save with disabled grouping.
trans-unit.source: How old records can be grouped. It means it will try to process all last X days of records to group them. Usually you want to have this number low (1-2) in order to avoid process already processed records, but you can set high value (by example world age) in order to process at once all records from some old save with disabled grouping.
trans-unit.target: كيف يمكن تجميع السجلات القديمة. هذا يعني أنها ستحاول معالجة جميع السجلات الخاصة بآخر X أيام لتجميعها. عادةً ما تريد أن يكون هذا الرقم منخفضًا (1-2) لتجنب معالجة السجلات التي تمت معالجتها بالفعل، ولكن يمكنك تعيين قيمة عالية (على سبيل المثال عمر العالم) لمعالجة جميع السجلات من بعض الحفظات القديمة دفعة واحدة مع تعطيل التجميع.

trans-unit.source: Chunk dimensions of the world along X-Z. Both dimensions must have the same value and be divisible by 4. World size has limits but they usually apply when world size bigger than 250x250. If you want size bigger -> then MaxBuildHeight must be less than 320. Example: Size 300 has 238 max height, 400 has 134, etc.
trans-unit.target: أبعاد أجزاء العالم على المحورين X-Z. يجب أن يكون لكلا البعدين نفس القيمة وأن يكونا قابلين للقسمة على 4. حجم العالم له حدود، لكنها عادةً ما تنطبق عندما يكون حجم العالم أكبر من 250x250. إذا كنت تريد حجمًا أكبر - >، فيجب أن يكون MaxBuildHeight أقل من 320. مثال: الحجم 300 له ارتفاع أقصى يبلغ 238، والحجم 400 له ارتفاع يبلغ 134، وهكذا.

trans-unit.id: Maximum height of the world citizens may build to. Can't be lowered after world creation. Note that values bigger than 160 will heavily increase CPU and RAM resources needed for world. Has hard limit for 320. Should not be lower than MaxGenerationHeight. World dimensions product ((Length * 10) * MaxBuildHeight * (Width * 10)) must be less than max value if INT, so values can be clamped to lower on server start.
trans-unit.source: Maximum height of the world citizens may build to. Can't be lowered after world creation. Note that values bigger than 160 will heavily increase CPU and RAM resources needed for world. Has hard limit for 320. Should not be lower than MaxGenerationHeight. World dimensions product ((Length * 10) * MaxBuildHeight * (Width * 10)) must be less than max value if INT, so values can be clamped to lower on server start.
trans-unit.target: الارتفاع الأقصى الذي يمكن لمواطني العالم البناء عليه. لا يمكن تخفيضه بعد إنشاء العالم. لاحظ أن القيم الأكبر من 160 ستزيد بشكل كبير من موارد وحدة المعالجة المركزية وذاكرة الوصول العشوائي اللازمة للعالم. له حد أقصى عند 320. يجب ألا يكون أقل من MaxGenerationHeight. يجب أن يكون حاصل ضرب أبعاد العالم ((الطول * 10) * MaxBuildHeight * (العرض * 10)) أقل من القيمة القصوى إذا كان INT، بحيث يمكن تقييد القيم إلى أقل عند بدء تشغيل الخادم.

trans-unit.source: Specifies the formula or curve that controls the shape of how the audio fades between the ConversationalDistance and the AudibleDistance. (1:InverseByDistance) - Fades voice quickly at first, buts slows down as you get further from conversational distance. trans-unit.id: Defines how the penalty percentage scales between the start and maximum pollution values. Possible values: Linear (penalty increases uniformly), Exponential (penalty increases slowly at first, then rapidly at high pollution), Logarithmic (penalty is strong at low pollution, then flattens at higher values), DoubleSigmoid (penalty increases strongly at low pollution, slows near mid-range, then increases strongly again near maximum pollution).
trans-unit.source: Defines how the penalty percentage scales between the start and maximum pollution values. Possible values: Linear (penalty increases uniformly), Exponential (penalty increases slowly at first, then rapidly at high pollution), Logarithmic (penalty is strong at low pollution, then flattens at higher values), DoubleSigmoid (penalty increases strongly at low pollution, slows near mid-range, then increases strongly again near maximum pollution).

trans-unit.id: This clause allows players to define in words what they would like done. When using this clause, the contract can no longer be auto-approved, and the client will have to approve it before accepting it. trans-unit.id:
This clause allows you to restrict the acceptance of a contract to only those that have a reputation equal to or greater than the defined amount.

There are two kinds of reputation you can specify here: 
 - Reputation, which is the sum of all player's ratings.
 - Relative Reputation, which is the sum of the opinions from players you have rated favorably (and who they have rated favorably, etc).

You can review the reputations of all players on the server through the citizen list, which displays players in reputation order, and displays reviews from other players in the reputation tooltip.
trans-unit.source:
This clause allows you to restrict the acceptance of a contract to only those that have a reputation equal to or greater than the defined amount.

There are two kinds of reputation you can specify here: 
 - Reputation, which is the sum of all player's ratings.
 - Relative Reputation, which is the sum of the opinions from players you have rated favorably (and who they have rated favorably, etc).

You can review the reputations of all players on the server through the citizen list, which displays players in reputation order, and displays reviews from other players in the reputation tooltip.

هناك نوعان من السمعة يمكنك تحديدهما هنا: 
 - السمعة، وهي مجموع تقييمات جميع اللاعبين.
 - السمعة النسبية، وهي مجموع آراء اللاعبين الذين قمت بتقييمهم بشكل إيجابي (والذين قاموا بتقييمهم بشكل إيجابي، وما إلى ذلك).

trans-unit.id:
Annexing a target requires paying them Claim Papers from the source settlement. Unlike resources, these 100% go to the foundation of the target without waste. The cost is determined per-non-abandoned citizen in the target.
In the case of annexing a Homestead, this number will be increased by the number of Homestead Support Claim Papers that are on the stake. This makes the support claims not only allow homesteads to claim more plots, but have more protection against annexation.
trans-unit.source:
Annexing a target requires paying them Claim Papers from the source settlement. Unlike resources, these 100% go to the foundation of the target without waste. The cost is determined per-non-abandoned citizen in the target.
In the case of annexing a Homestead, this number will be increased by the number of Homestead Support Claim Papers that are on the stake. This makes the support claims not only allow homesteads to claim more plots, but have more protection against annexation.

يتطلب ضم هدف ما دفع أوراق المطالبة من المستوطنة المصدر. على عكس الموارد، تذهب هذه الأوراق بنسبة 100٪ إلى تأسيس الهدف دون أي هدر. يتم تحديد التكلفة لكل مواطن غير مهجور في الهدف.
في حالة ضم مزرعة، سيتم زيادة هذا العدد بعدد أوراق المطالبة بدعم المزرعة الموجودة على المحك. وهذا يجعل مطالبات الدعم لا تسمح للمزارع بالمطالبة بمزيد من قطع الأراضي فحسب، بل توفر لها أيضًا مزيدًا من الحماية ضد الضم.

trans-unit.id:
The resources shown must exist in storage attached to an Embassy Desk that is assigned to the Settlement's jurisdiction. They must be accessible to the leader of the Settlement. The cost is determined per-non-abandoned citizen in the target.
Upon annexation, a percent of these will be given to the other party, and the rest destroyed as the cost of the annexation.
If all citizens of a target are 'Abandoned', no resources are needed.

السلامة هي أقصى درجة متانة يمكن إصلاح الكائن إليها، والتي تنخفض في كل مرة يتم إصلاحه. الإصلاح يرفع متانة العنصر إلى مستوى السلامة الحالي، لكن السلامة لا يمكن رفعها أبدًا، بل يمكن خفضها فقط.

trans-unit.id:
The resources shown must exist in storage attached to an Embassy Desk that is assigned to the Settlement's jurisdiction. They must be accessible to the leader of the Settlement.
Upon annexation, a percent of these will be given to the other party, and the rest destroyed as the cost of the annexation.
If all citizens of a target are 'Abandoned', no resources are needed.

trans-unit.id: Blocks must stay connected to the ground. A block that no longer touches the ground through other blocks falls: natural blocks fall as they are, constructed blocks fall and turn into garbage (see Salvage Share). Sideways connections count, so a bridge anchored at one end is still connected: whether it can actually hold is up to Constructed Blocks Need Support.
trans-unit.source: Blocks must stay connected to the ground. A block that no longer touches the ground through other blocks falls: natural blocks fall as they are, constructed blocks fall and turn into garbage (see Salvage Share). Sideways connections count, so a bridge anchored at one end is still connected: whether it can actually hold is up to Constructed Blocks Need Support.

trans-unit.id: Constructed blocks must hold themselves up, with two numbers shown in each block's tooltip. Horizontal support: how many blocks out a block can stick out sideways (held from the side or hanging) from a column standing on the ground. Supported weight: how much structural weight piled on it a block can carry, less the further out it is. A block past its horizontal support, or carrying more than it supports, cracks, then breaks with everything it was holding. A block resting on the block under it has no horizontal limit. Weight only goes down, toward the ground, through the blocks holding it. Building against rock anchors a construction; loose ground (dirt, sand, clay, gravel) does not. Natural blocks set on a construction, like a field on a roof, weigh on it.
trans-unit.source: Constructed blocks must hold themselves up, with two numbers shown in each block's tooltip. Horizontal support: how many blocks out a block can stick out sideways (held from the side or hanging) from a column standing on the ground. Supported weight: how much structural weight piled on it a block can carry, less the further out it is. A block past its horizontal support, or carrying more than it supports, cracks, then breaks with everything it was holding. A block resting on the block under it has no horizontal limit. Weight only goes down, toward the ground, through the blocks holding it. Building against rock anchors a construction; loose ground (dirt, sand, clay, gravel) does not. Natural blocks set on a construction, like a field on a roof, weigh on it.

trans-unit.id: Natural blocks that do not rest on solid ground all the way down (cave ceilings, overhangs, the rock above a tunnel) follow the horizontal support rule of constructed blocks with each rock's own horizontal support: a ceiling spans about twice it. Constructions standing on the ground hold them up, so pillars and props save a mine. Loose ground (dirt, sand, clay, gravel) keeps a slope: a free-standing pile higher than 2 blocks slides down, unless it rests on a rock or masonry ledge or is wedged between two solids. Fallen blocks keep their type. When off, natural blocks only fall when they are disconnected (see Disconnected Blocks Fall).
trans-unit.source: Natural blocks that do not rest on solid ground all the way down (cave ceilings, overhangs, the rock above a tunnel) follow the horizontal support rule of constructed blocks with each rock's own horizontal support: a ceiling spans about twice it. Constructions standing on the ground hold them up, so pillars and props save a mine. Loose ground (dirt, sand, clay, gravel) keeps a slope: a free-standing pile higher than 2 blocks slides down, unless it rests on a rock or masonry ledge or is wedged between two solids. Fallen blocks keep their type. When off, natural blocks only fall when they are disconnected (see Disconnected Blocks Fall).

trans-unit.id: Placed objects (tables, machines, storages) fall into a garbage bag, with all their contents, when the ground under them goes or when falling blocks land on them; the bag can be picked back up. When off, objects stay where they are, even in mid-air, and falling blocks land on top of them.

trans-unit.id: Rock standing on this many rock blocks counts as solid ground, for natural blocks and as an anchor for constructions: only the layers of rock just above a void can cave in, so a cave too wide brings down a slab this thick, then the next one over a narrower opening, until it settles into a vault, instead of the whole mountain above it. Loose ground never counts. 0: only rock in an unbroken column from bedrock is ground.
